chunks: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about something concerning tawhid, and he said:

Indeed Allah — blessed are His names by which He is called, and Exalted is He in the loftiness of His essence — is One. He singularized Himself with oneness in His uniqueness, then caused it to flow upon His creation.
So He is One, Samad, Holy. Everything worships Him and everything turns toward Him, and He encompasses all things in knowledge.

key_terms.التوحيد: Tawhid — divine unity, the foundational Islamic doctrine that God is absolutely one
key_terms.الصمد: Al-Samad — a Quranic divine name (112:2) meaning the Eternal Self-Sufficient, upon whom all depend
key_terms.القدوس: Al-Quddus — one of the Beautiful Names of God, meaning the All-Holy, transcending all deficiencies
key_terms.توحّد: Tawahhada — God's act of manifesting His absolute oneness unto Himself before extending it to creation
key_terms.كنهه: Kunhihi — the innermost essence/reality of a thing; referring to God's inscrutable essence

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the meaning of tawhid and al-Samad?
ai.summary: Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi asked Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) about tawhid (divine unity), and the Imam gave a profound theological response explaining that God's oneness is not merely a numerical attribute but an intrinsic, transcendent reality. The Imam then described how this divine oneness was made manifest in creation, and enumerated three of God's most essential attributes: al-Wahid (the One), al-Samad (the Eternal Self-Sufficient), and al-Quddus (the Holy). This hadith is particularly significant as it addresses one of the most advanced concepts in Shia theology — that God's names and attributes, while blessed and invoked in supplication, do not limit or qualify the absolute transcendence of His essence.
